items.title: Joint Gaussian coefficient law

source.anchor: Section 4.1.1, Angular functions, the independent draws before Eq. (14) and the joint direct sum and law after Eq. (15)
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, CC BY 4.0. Samplinglib explanation and formalization; no endorsement implied.

items.statement: Draw independent centered identity-covariance Gaussian tensors Ξ_i,p in the stated ordered tensor spaces. Collect them into the Euclidean direct sum. The collected vector has its centered identity-covariance Gaussian law. Equivalently, grouping the coordinates of that joint Gaussian returns the product of the block standard Gaussian laws.
assumptions: In the paper n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated finite law holds for all positive integer n and natural h; admissibility is not generalized.
The independent standard Gaussian tensor blocks range over levels i=0,…,h and even degrees p=4,6,…,P. Each block retains the ordered tensor carrier with n^(pS_i) coordinates.
The law is unconditioned. The family carrier has the product measurable structure; the Euclidean geometry is on the ℓ² direct sum, not the default dependent-function norm.

obligations.label: Preserve every ordered level/degree coefficient coordinate
Derive the measurable unconditioned joint-to-product law

bindings.boundary: Unconditioned joint coefficient law and its block marginals and mutual independence only. Degree sums, radial/zero-block fields, adaptive and conditional laws, admissibility, normalizer moments and all main lower bounds remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: Sufficiently large n and the prescribed h
assumption_deltas.reason: The finite identity does not use the growth regime. Nothing extends the parameter bounds or admissible instances.

assumption_deltas.source: Independent standard Gaussians on the ordered tensor blocks, collected into the joint Euclidean law
assumption_deltas.lean: Exact measurable inverse regrouping of the flat stdGaussian into their product
assumption_deltas.reason: The maps keep every entry unchanged and are inverses. The bare dependent Pi only serves as a measurable product; no sup-norm isometry is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Even degrees 4 through P and levels 0 through h with exact K and P
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite degree subtype and level index with the same bounds and constants
assumption_deltas.reason: Fin(P+1) includes P, the filter keeps parity and the lower endpoint, and each block has all ordered tensor slots.
